candidates.title: Rizal Park entrance
candidates.description: En route to the Intramuros district, we pass the main entrance to Rizal Park, an important green lung in the city. We are now in the Ermita district of Manila. A bevy of lovely beauties emerges from the park, much to my delight. We did not halt here, as we were short of time, but we did make a photo stop to see the Rizal Monument, located just round the corner at one of the side entrances to the park. The ice cream vendor with his tricycle seen at the gate was playing an electronic tune (tink-tonk-tink-tink-- of the type you hear on the telephone when someone puts you on hold) which seemed to the the Philippines standard for ice cream vendors all over the country. I'd heard this tune in Davao, Puerto Princesa, Bohol and now here in Manila. The kid accompanying me, my foster daughter, had some explanation for it (the name of the song) but I did not note that down. (Manila, Philippines, May 2013)
candidates.creator: shankar s.

candidates.title: Rizal Park stage on San Pedro shopping street
candidates.description: We then took a taxi back into downtown Davao, to the San Pedro shopping street. San Pedro St. is considered to be the oldest street in Davao city. Unfortunately, thanks to a just concluded feverish election campaign, the local politicos had promised to make up for their excesses by saving power. Due to tis, much of the street lighting had been switched off and we had to rely on the lights from the many hand cards, many of which were unlit anyway. Frankly, had it not been for my delightful travel companions, I might never have ventured into that street in the dark. The recently stopped rain made things darker still. Here is an overview of the shopping area with greatly curtailed street lighting. Structure seen here is the Rizal Park stage on San Pedro in Davao. Love the fabulous metal eagle motif atop the shed.  (Davao, Philippines, May 2013)
candidates.creator: shankar s.

candidates.title: Jose Rizal : National Hero with a Style
candidates.description:
Rizal Park, Davao City, Philippines

“Rizal" is a compulsory course in school, but few teachers make Rizal's novels interesting. If students are taught to enjoy Rizal's works as literature instead of as a lodemine of 'patriotic' allusions I am sure they would not mind reading and rereading the 'Noli me Tangere'.” 
― Ambeth R. Ocampo
candidates.creator: Bro. Jeffrey  Pioquinto, SJ
